author: high4
claim: A red-blue coloring of the complete graph on five vertices with no monochromatic triangle is obtained by coloring a 5-cycle red and its complement blue.
evidence: Label the vertices 0,1,2,3,4 cyclically. Color 01,12,23,34,40 red and color the other five edges 02,24,41,13,30 blue. The red edges form exactly the 5-cycle 0-1-2-3-4-0. The blue edges form exactly the 5-cycle 0-2-4-1-3-0. A 5-cycle has no triangle: among any three vertices, if all three mutual edges belonged to a cycle, every selected vertex would have both cycle-neighbors selected, forcing closure under repeatedly taking cycle-neighbors and hence all five vertices would be selected, a contradiction. Thus neither color class contains a triangle.

links.example: On five cyclically labelled vertices, use the cycle edges in one color and all remaining edges in the other.
links.why_relevant: It proves the lower bound R(3,3)>5.
assumptions_satisfied: Every edge of the complete graph on five vertices receives exactly one of red and blue.
links.where_assumptions_take_effect: The complement of a 5-cycle is again a 5-cycle.
